how_to_apply: Artifact read (raw HTML) → apply each old→new replacement exactly once → Artifact publish with url → then the owner re-pins in the UI (viewers see a pinned earlier version). Publishing is owner-gated.

patch.where: HTML line 14 (opening box, 'People named here who are accused of nothing') — KNOWN DEFECT 1
patch.old: Amber Robinson and Matthew Robinson appear only as elimination-sample donors — people whose profiles are obtained precisely so they can be identified and set aside — sought because they were associated with the premises, not as suspects. No inference about any of them may be drawn from this page.
patch.new: Amber Robinson and Matthew Robinson are elimination-sample donors — people whose DNA profiles are obtained precisely so they can be identified and set aside — sought because they were associated with the premises and not as suspects. The record does contain support-for-inclusion results naming two of the three people named here: Matthew Robinson on ATF items 1.4 (the bolt) and 1.6 (the barrel), and Lance Twiggs on swabs of the buttons of the Dremel rotary tool and other areas of that tool. A “support for inclusion” statement is not a source attribution — the ATF analyst corrected counsel’s contrary phrasing three times and counsel expressly accepted the correction. Two things travel with those results: defence counsel’s framing, put in a leading question and assented to by the witness — “not because he’s a suspect, but because he’s associated with that premise” — and the analyst’s own words about household items, “it’s reasonable to assume that anyone living in the household could have contributed to DNA on an object found in that household.” No inference about any of them may be drawn from this page.

patch.old: Everything here is what a witness said under oath. No laboratory report has been read directly — every figure reaches this summary through a witness reading or describing a document aloud in court.
patch.new: Almost everything here is what a witness said under oath. The exceptions are the four-report block in §06 and all of §07, which come instead from a defence discovery letter filed with the court. One laboratory report has been read directly — the ATF firearms report of 17 September 2025 — and it is not the source of any DNA figure here: every DNA figure below still reaches this summary through a witness describing or reading a document aloud in court, because every DNA report from both laboratories remains unread.

patch.where: HTML line 107 (§06 'This is a gap in the record')
patch.old: This was a probable-cause hearing, not a trial. A negative fingerprint result on the rifle is exactly the kind of finding neither side had reason to raise. Absence here is weak evidence of absence.
patch.new: This was a probable-cause hearing, not a trial. A negative fingerprint result on the rifle is the kind of finding the State had no reason to raise — it called no forensic examiner and proceeded by stipulation — though the defence, which held all four latent print reports, had formally sought the ATF fingerprint specialist's live testimony. Absence here is weak evidence of absence, and weaker on the State's side than on the defence's.
